newsitem.title: USA: Nissan's Infiniti cuts price of J30 by $2,250.
newsitem.headline: Nissan's Infiniti cuts price of J30 by $2,250.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co. Ltd.'s Infiniti luxury car division Monday slashed the base sticker price of its J30 luxury sedan for the second time in less than five months, reducing it another $2,250 to $33,500.
The price cut for the new 1997-1/2 J30 comes on top of a $4,170 reduction when the automaker introduced the 1997 model in July. The new price is 16 percent below the 1996 model's price of $39,920.

The company said the price drop is in keeping with its "consumer-based pricing" philosophy -- an effort to bring sticker prices in line with actual transaction prices. The price includes delivery charges of $495.

"Last June, we lowered the MSRP on a number of our Infiniti luxury vehicles in order to bring them in closer alignment with what consumers are likely to pay," Tom Eastwood, Infiniti vice president, said in a statement.

Changes in the new 1997-1/2 J30 are minimal compared to the 1997 model. They include an improved audio system and a new pewter exterior colour, which replaces the previous beige and pebble, Infiniti said.
